definitions.explanation: the basement floor(s) of Japanese department stores that contain high-quality food shops, delicatessens, and confectioneries

examples.japanese: デパ{地下|ちか}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦お{弁当|べんとう}→お弁当：02864_obentou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}った→買う：00489_kau⟧。
examples.english: I bought a bento at the department store food hall.

examples.japanese: デパ{地下|ちか}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦スイーツ→スイーツ：27370_suiitsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{美味|おい}しい→美味しい：00740_oishii⟧。
examples.english: The sweets at the department store basement are delicious.

examples.japanese: ⟦{夕方|ゆうがた}→夕方：01010_yuugata⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧デパ{地下|ちか}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{混|こ}んでいる→混む：02574_komu⟧。
examples.english: The department store food hall is crowded in the evening.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
デパ{地下|ちか} = ⟦デパート→デパート：01022_depaato⟧ (department store) + ⟦{地下|ちか}→地下：03429_chika⟧ (basement). It's a blend word (portmanteau) coined to describe the food floors in Japanese department stores.

WHAT YOU'LL FIND:
- ⟦{惣菜|そうざい}→惣菜：05827_souzai⟧ - prepared foods, deli items
- ⟦{弁当|べんとう}→弁当：01014_bentou⟧ - bento boxes
- ⟦{和菓子|わがし}→和菓子：04962_wagashi⟧ / ⟦{洋菓子|ようがし}→洋菓子：04998_yougashi⟧ - Japanese/Western confections
- ⟦{精肉|せいにく}→精肉：14826_seiniku⟧ / ⟦{鮮魚|せんぎょ}→鮮魚：16483_sengyo⟧ - meat/fish
- ⟦{名店|めいてん}→名店：21511_meiten⟧ - famous restaurant branches
- ⟦{手土産|てみやげ}→手土産：08353_temiyage⟧ - gift items

CULTURAL NOTE:
- デパ{地下|ちか} is known for high-quality but often expensive food
- ⟦{閉店|へいてん}→閉店：09698_heiten⟧⟦セール→セール：07780_seeru⟧ (closing time sales) offer discounts on perishables before closing
- Popular for buying ⟦{手土産|てみやげ}→手土産：08353_temiyage⟧ (gifts) when visiting someone
